subject: Sizing for hybrid reserved + burst — traffic breakdown & risk triggers
messages:
From: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@stellarsolutions.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stellarsolutions.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sizing for our pilot - hybrid reserved + burst?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we discussed, Stellar is evaluating a hybrid approach: a baseline reserved pool for steady daytime traffic and a burst buffer for marketing pushes / product launches. Before we lock numbers with finance, we need a concise questionnaire so we can hand ownership to our infra team.

High-level asks from our side:
- Rough tokens/second we should expect during weekday business hours (EST) for the baseline pool.
- Expected peak token/s during a 30–90 minute marketing spike.
- How you recommend sizing reservation to avoid throttling while keeping cost predictable.
- What triggers we should use to flip from reserved -> burst and any automatic fallback hooks.

I attached a short CSV export of a recent week of traffic (stellars_burst_report.csv) — sample includes 1,000 sessions with request/response token counts and timestamps. Can you share a short questionnaire or a template we can fill and return by EOD Wednesday?

Sandra
Sandra Liu
Head of Platform Operations
Stellar Solutions

[attachment: stellars_burst_report.csv (csv, 78KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@stellarsolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sizing for our pilot - hybrid reserved + burst?

Hi Sandra — thanks for the data and the clear list. I reviewed the CSV quickly and sketched a short questionnaire below to capture the details we need to produce an accurate reserved + burst sizing recommendation. If you can fill this out (or point to owners for each row) we’ll return a recommended capacity mix and a simple commit/burst policy doc (PDF) by Thursday.

Redwood pre-sales sizing questionnaire (short):
1) Traffic profile
  - Typical average requests per minute (RPM) during business hours (Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 local): [numeric]
  - Average prompt tokens / request and average response tokens: [prompt_tokens, response_tokens]
  - Hourly variance: percentiles (p50/p90/p99) for requests/minute and tokens/request (if available)

2) Session and concurrency
  - Typical session duration (seconds) for interactive flows vs batch flows
  - Max concurrent sessions observed in past 30 days (or estimate)
  - Session affinity needs (must stay on same model instance / ok to shard)

3) Burst characteristics
  - Example burst scenarios (marketing push / feature launch) with duration and multipliers (e.g., 5x baseline for 45 minutes)
  - Desired SLAs during bursts (p95 latency target, acceptable error rate)

4) Model/response characteristics
  - Model family / size you intend to serve (e.g., Llama-3-70B, open model)
  - Do you plan to use caching or prefix KV-cache for repeated prompts?
  - Percent of requests requiring streaming vs full-response generation

5) Operational constraints
  - Cost guardrails: max monthly cost for inference (optional)
  - Regions where traffic must run (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU)
  - Compliance needs (data residency, logging retention)

Quick note on triggers: Redwood recommends a hybrid policy where reserved capacity handles p90 of steady-state and burst elastic capacity is used for short windows beyond that. Trigger options we propose:
- Autoscale start when 5-minute token-rate exceeds reserved-capacity-utilization threshold (e.g., 85%)
- Burst duration cap (e.g., 2 hours) with automatic cooldown to avoid runaway costs
- Fallback chain: preferred model -> smaller quantized model -> queued responses with retry headers

Attachments: I’ll attach a one-page proposal after you send the completed questionnaire. If helpful, Marissa can run the quick modeling against the CSV and return an explicit GPU map (GPUs required, expected concurrency per GPU) — looping her in.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick model run on Stellar CSV

Priyom / Karthik —
I pulled the sample CSV and ran a rapid simulation using Redwood’s sizing tool. High-level observations:
- Baseline (p90) token-rate translates to ~12 sustained inference vGPUs (A100-equivalent) if they use a 70B-class model with typical prompt+response length ~400 tokens.
- Peak bursts in CSV (there’s an obvious 50-minute marketing spike) would need an additional 18 vGPUs to maintain p95 latency < 600ms with continuous batching.
- If they accept quantized 8-bit model variants for burst mode, extra vGPU need drops to ~10.

Risk and recommendation:
- Suggest we size reserved pool at ~60% of p90 to provide headroom for short bursts and use burst capacity for the remaining. This keeps monthly committed costs lower while still minimizing throttling risk.
- Define automatic trigger: 3 consecutive 1-minute windows > 80% reserved utilization -> spin up burst nodes. Cooldown: 20 minutes after utilization drops below 60%.
- For billing/commit terms, propose a 6-month reserved commit + credit for first two spike hours/month free for first quarter to soften their initial cost.

I can convert this into a short table (GPU map per scenario) and include it in the PDF proposal. Karthik — can you sanity check the vGPU numbers (I used conservative token processing rate = 1200 tokens/sec per vGPU for 70B float32)?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sizing for our pilot - hybrid reserved + burst?

Hi Sandra — thanks again for the data. Attached is a short recommendation and a GPU map for three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Key highlights:
- Recommended reserved commit: 8 vGPUs (covers ~60% of p90 steady-state)
- Burst buffer: ability to scale +10 vGPUs on demand (quantized 8-bit variant) with a 20-minute cooldown rule
- Trigger: 3 consecutive 1-minute windows above 80% reserved utilization to start burst flow; automatic teardown after sustained <60% for 20 minutes
- Fallback policy: auto-fallback to quantized model, then to queued short responses if latency targets cannot be met

Next steps:
1) If this looks reasonable, sign the attached short SOW (two-page) and we’ll reserve the commit in pricing.
2) We can schedule a 30-minute ops review with your infra team to validate autoscale hooks and alerting (I propose Tue/Thu next week).

I attached redwood_hybrid_proposal_v1.pdf with the GPU map and cost sensitivity table. Let me know if you want different model family assumptions.

Best,
Priyom

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
